newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares little changed market summer pause.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares little changed market summer pause.

text.p: Leading Russian shares started lower in desultory morning trade on Thursday, although some later picked up a few points, and traders said the market looked set to put its feet up at least for next week as brokers and investors go on vacation.
The Russian Trading System opened at 506.63, barely lower than Wednesday's closing 508.12.

"Finally, the market is going down, which I think is overdue," said Dan Rapoport, director of sales at Centreinvest Securities. "I see some profit taking by local brokers, volumes under 60 million for the next couple of days, people are going on vacation -- and the market needs time to pause."
At 0845 GMT national power company UES had ticked up to $0.4175 from $0.4150 on Wednesday, while oil company LUKoil firmed to $22.65 from $22.40.

International long-distance carrier Rostelekom was barely changed at $4.90 after $4.89, and Rapoport, who said he saw lower levels by the end of the trading session, saw selling pressure in the telecoms sector for the next few days.

Creditanstalt Grant sales director Tad Berger said fund managers had made most Russian allocations and were looking for better value in the run-up to the third quarter. But he said the market would not necessarily continue to sink even though it was likely to remain quiet for most of August.
"I don't see a lot of upward trend in the blue chips, but they will be cycling around, there will be repositioning going on," he said.
